description:
draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.7 (line 1417 onward) defines four extra arguments on top of the standard /get for CalendarEvent:
- recurrenceOverridesBefore: UTCDateTime|null — filter overrides by date
- recurrenceOverridesAfter: UTCDateTime|null — filter overrides by date
- reduceParticipants: Boolean — omit non-owner participants
- timeZone: TimeZoneId (default 'Etc/UTC') — used to compute utcStart/utcEnd for floating events

src/event.rs:24-61 (handle_calendar_event_get) reads the request, decides whether utcStart/utcEnd are wanted, then forwards args verbatim to jmap_server::handlers::handle_get. The four §5.7 extra args are NEVER extracted from the args object and NEVER passed to the backend. Specifically:
- recurrenceOverridesBefore/After: not parsed at all; the backend has no path to receive them
- reduceParticipants: not parsed at all
- timeZone: src/event.rs:48 calls compute_utc_times(account_id, event, None) — passes hardcoded None for tz_hint, ignoring whatever timeZone the client sent

PLAN.md §7 explicitly described a CalendarEventGetArgs struct that should be passed to the backend method get_calendar_events. That struct does not exist in src/backend.rs.

Wire impact: a compliant client calling CalendarEvent/get with reduceParticipants:true gets back the full participant list anyway. A client requesting utcStart with timeZone:'America/New_York' for a floating event gets utcStart computed using a default tz instead.

Fix: add CalendarEventGetArgs (or extend CalendarsBackend) to receive the four args, parse them in handle_calendar_event_get, pass to backend. Pass the parsed timeZone to compute_utc_times in place of the hardcoded None.

Test gap: there are no inline tests covering any of these four args. Add at minimum: (a) a test that reduceParticipants:true makes it to the backend, (b) a test that timeZone is forwarded to compute_utc_times.
title: CalendarEvent/get §5.7 extra args silently dropped (recurrenceOverridesBefore/After, reduceParticipants, timeZone)
